findings.summary: result_is_stale() compares ScientificInputs.signature with exact float equality, but current_inputs is recomputed each rerun by round-tripping the field value through the selected display unit (K<->degF, Pa<->psi/bar); this round trip is not bit-exact for ~50% of realistic temperature values (verified directly against validate_scientific_inputs, e.g. 373.7993794602593 K -> degF -> 373.79937946025933 K), so merely switching the temperature (or pressure) display unit with no physical change frequently marks an already-calculated, unchanged result as stale and disables its downloads. This directly contradicts this PR's own new documentation ('does not... make a current scientific result stale') and is not caught by the existing regression test because that test's fixed 300 K/5 MPa case happens to round-trip exactly through every supported unit.

safe_defer.summary: _presentation_figure's hovertemplate unit-label substitution uses a literal string .replace(" K", ...).replace(" Pa", ...) rather than a structured template; currently safe for all existing hover strings but fragile against future wording changes in the frozen plotting module.
Sweep-table pressure display rounds to a fixed 5 decimal digits regardless of the selected unit's magnitude (fine for Pa, imprecise-looking for psi/bar); cosmetic only.

I tried to falsify this (temperature sweeps ending within 1e-13 K of absolute zero) and could not. ## Finding: unit switching frequently causes a false "stale result" (and blocks exports) — contradicts the PR's own documentation The work package's own updated documentation states: *"Changing a unit converts the editable value and preserves the physical state; it does not run a calculation or make a current scientific result stale"* and *"Unit-only changes therefore redraw existing results without recomputing or changing their scientific identity."* This is false for a large fraction of real inputs. `result_is_stale` (`state.py:161`) compares `ScientificInputs.signature` — an exact tuple of `(mole_fractions, temperature_k, pressure_pa)` — with `!=`. `current_inputs` is recomputed on *every* rerun by re-parsing whatever is currently sitting in the (possibly unit-converted) text field through `validate_scientific_inputs`. Switching the unit selector round-trips the value through `convert_temperature`/`convert_pressure` and then re-parses it back to SI — and IEEE-754 double arithmetic does not guarantee that round trip returns the bit-identical float it started from. I verified this directly against the production `validate_scientific_inputs` function (not a hand-built reference), submitting a case and then only switching display units without touching the physical value: ``` submitted = validate_scientific_inputs((50,0,50), 305.7, 12.34) # via K / MPa current = validate_scientific_inputs((50,0,50), t_f, p_psi, # same case, via °F / psi temperature_unit=FAHRENHEIT, pressure_unit=PSI) ``` Across 20,000 random realistic `(temperature_k, pressure_mpa)` pairs, **50.2% of temperature signatures mismatched by 1 ULP after a K→°F→K round trip** (e.g. `373.7993794602593` → `373.79937946025933`), even though the physical state is unchanged. Because `result_is_stale` uses exact equality, this means: for roughly half of arbitrary user inputs, merely clicking the temperature-unit selector to °F — with no other change — will make the UI show *"Stale result — submitted scientific inputs changed. Run this calculation again before use,"* and, per the app's own stale-handling logic, disable the CSV/JSON download buttons until the user needlessly resubmits. This propagates to every cached result type gated the same way (flash, envelope, critical, critical_scan, sweep), since they all key off the same `current_inputs`/signature comparison. The existing regression test for exactly this behavior, `test_presentation_unit_change_does_not_stale_a_calculated_result` (`tests/test_app_streamlit.py:100`), passes only because it happens to use the suite's canonical default case (300 K / 5 MPa via °C/bar), and I confirmed by direct computation that this specific value round-trips exactly through all four supported units — it is not representative. Tellingly, a *different* test in the same file (`test_field_unit_selection_preserves_state_and_submits_si_to_engine`, line 90) already had to use `pytest.approx(300.0, abs=1e-13)` rather than exact equality for the same 300 K value through Fahrenheit for the *submission* path — i.e. the imprecision was empirically visible to the builder in one place but its consequence for the staleness comparison a few lines away was not connected. This doesn't corrupt any scientific result (the flash/envelope/critical numbers themselves are still exactly correct once actually computed) and doesn't touch the frozen engine, so it isn't an "A"-level scientific-integrity defect. But it's a real, easily-reproduced functional regression that defeats a central, explicitly documented promise of this specific work package, and will visibly misbehave for ordinary users switching to Fahrenheit.
